title: Reading Drill — Testing a train stop announcement — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Testing a train stop announcement — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Ravensmere, work on customers confusing stations with similar names had already produced a small collection of short listening trials. The station announcer used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: the proportion of stops identified correctly.

**B** The group kept an added neighbourhood reference for the new trial, which was planned to run for seven weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that background conversations should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
